target.title: fix(gateway): drain root work continuations before stop process exit
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105697

When a gateway process receives a direct stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT without a restart intent), any `session_end` plugin hooks that were already started by session reset/delete/compaction may be truncated before they complete. This happens because the session is removed from the shutdown tracker synchronously before the hook fires asynchronously via `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation`, and the direct-stop path (`handleStopAfterServerClose`) exits the process without waiting for these continuations to settle. Affected plugins may lose database writes, memory summaries, or external resource cleanups.

#### Why This Change Was Made

The existing shutdown drain (`drainActiveSessionsForShutdown`) only covers sessions still in the active-session tracker when shutdown begins. Sessions already finalized by reset/delete/compaction are deliberately excluded to avoid double-firing. Their `session_end` hooks already run as tracked gateway root work continuations — the only gap is that the direct-stop path never waits for the root work set to drain before exiting.

Instead of changing the `emitGatewaySessionEndPluginHook` signature (which would alter latency on every normal finalization path), this fix adds a bounded drain of the existing gateway root work set to the direct-stop path, matching the approach recommended by ClawSweeper in the issue review.

The drain uses a referenced `setTimeout` poll loop (not `.unref()`) so that the polling timer keeps the Node.js event loop alive during the wait. The wait is bounded at 2 seconds, and the caller always invokes `exitProcess(0)` after the drain returns, so a stuck hook cannot block shutdown indefinitely. Per review clarification: the force-exit watchdog is cleared at line 705 of `run-loop.ts` before `handleStopAfterServerClose` is entered at line 710, so the drain does not depend on the watchdog — it is self-bounded by its own referenced timer and the unconditional `exitProcess(0)` that follows.

#### User Impact

No visible impact under normal operation. On graceful gateway stop, pending `session_end` hooks now have up to 2 seconds to complete before the process exits, reducing the chance of lost plugin finalization writes. The wait is bounded to 2 seconds with a referenced timer, and the caller unconditionally calls `exitProcess(0)` after the drain returns (even on timeout), so a stuck hook cannot block shutdown.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors on changed files
- **Unit tests:**
  ```
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts

  ✓ |unit| src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts (17 tests)
  ✓ |cli|  src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts (45 tests)

  Test Files  2 passed (2)
       Tests  62 passed (62)
  ```
  - `gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 17 tests pass (+4: `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` success / timeout / immediate zero-count / poll-and-release)
  - `run-loop.test.ts` — 45 tests pass (+2: direct-stop drains root work before exit; warns and still exits on drain timeout; +1 mock fix)
- **Change scope:** 4 files, +116 lines
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.ts` — new `waitForGatewayRootWorkDrain` helper (referenced poll, no `.unref()`)
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts` — drain call in `handleStopAfterServerClose` before `exitProcess(0)`
  - `src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts` — 4 new tests for drain helper
  - `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.test.ts` — 2 new regression tests + mock fix
  - Directory scope: `src/cli`, `src/process` — no config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface affected
- **No new dependencies** — reuses existing `getActiveGatewayRootWorkCount`
- **ClawSweeper P1 fix:** removed `.unref()` from the drain poll loop. The referenced `setTimeout` keeps the event loop alive during the bounded wait, so Node cannot exit naturally before the next poll fires. The 2-second timeout and caller's `exitProcess(0)` guarantee no infinite hang.
- **Process-level proof:** spawned real child processes exercising the gateway work-admission module under SIGTERM at runtime. Each child process simulates the exact session-reset-service flow: acquire root admission → spawn fire-and-forget `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkContinuation` (tracked in `activeRootWork`) → release root → only continuation remains tracked. The parent sends SIGTERM mid-hook, then checks that every side-effect file exists after the child exits.

```
=== Gateway Stop Root Work Drain — Process-Level Proof ===

[Case 1] No pending hooks — drain returns immediately, clean exit
  exit code=0, elapsed=11ms
  2 passed so far

[Case 2] One pending 350ms hook — SIGTERM, drain waits, hook writes file, exit 0
  exit code=0, elapsed=261ms
  sentinel: completed at 1783921819708
  6 passed / 0 failed so far

[Case 3] Stuck hook (never releases) — drain times out, exits anyway
  exit code=0, elapsed=1017ms
  stderr: drain timed out with 1 pending
  9 passed / 0 failed so far

[Case 4] Two concurrent hooks (150ms + 350ms) — drain waits for slowest
  exit code=0, elapsed=362ms
  fast: completed at 1783921821572
  slow: completed at 1783921821772
  14 passed / 0 failed so far

=== Results: 14 passed / 0 failed ===
```

- **Case 1:** empty queue → drain returns true immediately (11ms)
- **Case 2:** 350ms hook mid-flight when SIGTERM arrives → drain blocks until hook writes sentinel file and releases continuation (~261ms), sentinel confirmed on disk after child exit
- **Case 3:** never-releasing continuation → drain returns false after 1s timeout, process still exits cleanly (code 0)
- **Case 4:** two concurrent hooks (150ms + 350ms) → drain waits for slowest (362ms), both sentinel files confirmed on disk
